summary.headline: Minda Corp Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR 1,704 crore (+29% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 203 crore at 11.9% margin and PAT of INR 124 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly and full-year revenue, EBITDA and PAT for Minda Corporation, with Q4 revenue up 29% YoY and FY26 revenue up 22.3% to INR 6,185 crore. Full-year PAT rose 40.3% to INR 358 crore, helped by higher associate income from Flash Electronics and lower interest costs. Management highlighted new JVs (Turntide, Toyodenso), the planned consolidation of Minda VAST from FY27, and a FY27 capex plan of INR 400-450 crore. Commodity inflation (copper, zinc, aluminium up 30-40% through the year) is largely passed through to customers, though management flagged some EBITDA-margin drag from the lag.

financial_highlights.value: INR 81 crore (Flash ~INR 70 crore, Furukawa ~INR 8 crore, Minda VAST ~INR 5 crore, EVQ nil)
Revenue INR 1,803 crore, EBITDA INR 310 crore (17.2%), PAT INR 137 crore (7.6%)

segments.name: Wiring harness
segments.commentary: Largest product at 31% of FY26 revenue; in-house division currently fulfils about 18-19% of Minda Corporation's requirement for connectors and couplers. Share gains came mainly from 2W, 3W and CV.

segments.name: Vehicle access / Instrument clusters
segments.commentary: Vehicle access 22% and cluster 17% of FY26 revenue. Multiple TFT cluster orders (3-inch to 15-inch) won; some SOPs are coming in across PV, CV, 2W, and exports.

segments.name: Die casting
segments.commentary: 15% of FY26 revenue. Noida plant operational; fifth plant in Pune under commissioning with about 18 months to completion, export-focused.

segments.name: Mobility mix
segments.commentary: 2W/3W 48%, CV 28%, PV 14%, aftermarket about 10% of FY26 revenue. Management targets 25% PV share, helped by VAST consolidation.

segments.name: Flash Electronics (associate)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 493 crore, FY26 INR 1,803 crore; EBITDA margin 18% in Q4. Q4 PAT rise attributed to export metallics orders, higher utilisation and lower interest cost.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal revenue guidance; guiding principle is growth at least 50% above industry, implying 15%+ revenue growth if industry grows ~10%.

Management said 19-20% growth from the INR 9,000-odd crore group base would be enough to reach the INR 17,500 crore FY30 vision (group level, incl. Flash and VAST); long-term target also 12.5% EBITDA margin.
PV segment at overall Minda Corporation level expected to grow north of 20% in FY27 (including VAST).
FY27 capex expected at INR 400-450 crore, versus INR 350-400 crore historically.
Commodity pressure expected to persist at least through next quarter until geopolitical situation eases; pass-through contracts should protect profit but may dent EBITDA margin.
Sunroof mass production in next 4-5 months, FY28 first full year; switches JV SOP around Q4 FY27 with FY29 as first peak year; Turntide SOP expected within FY27.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was a record INR 413 crore; FY27 capex guided at INR 400-450 crore.
Group capacity utilisation averages about 75-80%, varying by plant.
Minda Instruments' second plant under commissioning, expected ready by Q1 FY27 (for advanced cluster and cockpit electronics).
Die casting: Noida plant operational; Pune fifth plant under commissioning, about 18 months from now, mainly for exports.
Company acquired several industrial land parcels in FY26 for future plants.
demand_pricing: Industry context: Q4 FY26 2W up about 21% YoY, PV up about 11.3% (record), CV up about 20%, tractors up over 37%.
Minda grew 2W volumes over 26%, outperforming industry by about 12 points; PV grew over 12%; CV about 25%; exports also grew.
About 12-13 percentage points of the 29% Q4 growth came from premiumisation and new products; the rest from customer penetration and new customers.
Commodities (copper, zinc, aluminium) rose 30-40% through the year; most contracts are pass-through, with some EBITDA margin impact.
Lifetime order book: INR 3,500 crore booked in Q4 and over INR 10,000 crore in FY26 (about 20% exports); order lives typically 48-60 months.
Wiring harness kit value rises about 20% a year on average, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of FY26 INR 81 crore associate income and VAST financials?
qa_highlights.answer: Flash ~INR 70 crore, Furukawa ~INR 8 crore, VAST ~INR 5 crore, EVQ nil. VAST FY26 revenue about INR 500 crore (>90% PV) with ~7% EBITDA margin, expected to improve.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex and FY27 growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex expected at INR 400-450 crore. Management does not give revenue guidance, but targets growth at least 50% above industry (15%+ if industry grows ~10%).

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 17,500 crore FY30 vision on a group basis, and is 20%+ growth in FY27 needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed as group-level consolidated, including Flash, VAST and inorganic/JV opportunities. Management said 19-20% growth from the INR 9,000-odd crore group base keeps it on track.

qa_highlights.question: Margin impact from commodity and labour cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodities are largely pass-through, so profit should be protected, though EBITDA margin will see some impact. Management expects commodity pressure to persist at least one more quarter; labour cost rise in UP and Haryana is being offset by productivity and controlled hiring.

qa_highlights.question: Turntide JV scope and SOP timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Turntide brings axial flux motor technology; Flash covers low-threshold controllers and Turntide higher-threshold 3W/CV controllers. Motor controller orders won with SOP in about 5-6 months; existing businesses transfer in 3-4 months. Motor orders in advanced discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline and R&D levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the ~180 bps QoQ gross margin decline to higher RM costs and said people, conversion and power cost savings have helped hold EBITDA margin.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (copper, zinc, aluminium) and possible lag in pass-through could weigh on EBITDA margin; management expects no cooling at least in the next quarter.
Labour cost increases from 1 April 2026 in UP and Haryana; management says it will offset through productivity, but other states' reactions are uncertain.
FY30 INR 17,500 crore vision needs roughly 19-20% annual growth, and relies on JVs, M&A and consolidations not yet fully defined.
Ramp-up timing of Turntide (SOP FY27), switches JV (SOP around Q4 FY27, FY29 peak) and sunroof (mass production in 4-5 months) and Pune die casting plant (about 18 months).
Flash Electronics' Q4 PAT jump was partly due to lower interest cost and export orders; sustainability not confirmed.
Gross margin fell about 180 bps QoQ in Q4 per an analyst; management did not give a specific recovery timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order wins and the FY30 vision, with management repeatedly calling the quarter a record. More cautious on commodity and labour-cost outlook, and evasive on specifics for the Turntide motor orders (citing confidentiality) and on the CV outperformance multiple.
key_quotes: So, the Passenger Vehicle segment at the overall Minda Corporation level will grow north of 20%.
So we have kept the long-term vision in mind for 2030 to deliver INR 17,500 crores top line with 12.5% EBITDA margin.
So any escalation should not necessarily eat up our margin.
We are looking at 4-year window to deliver INR 17,500 crores number.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 15%+ (at least 1.5x a ~10% industry), backed by a INR 3,500 crore Q4 order booking and over INR 10,000 crore in FY26, plus FY27 capex of INR 400-450 crore and a Minda Instruments plant due ready in Q1 FY27; no explicit capacity-to-revenue bridge given.
